items.title: [ScienceDaily] Alaska’s monster tsunami sent water 1,580 feet up a mountain
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area. Scientists discovered that the disaster was preceded by several warning signs, including rapid glacier retreat, heavy rainfall, and thousands of tiny seismic tremors. As glaciers retreat, similar disasters could become a growing danger in mountainous coastal regions.

Physicists have discovered a strange new state of quantum matter in which ultracold atoms defy familiar organizational rules, forming a highly excited yet surprisingly orderly configuration called a "fractional Fermi sea." The discovery challenges established quantum theories and hints at exotic quasiparticles that scientists have dubbed potential "super-Fermions."

items.title: [israelnationalnews.com] Canadian military identifies four killed as Wainwright fire inquiry continues
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The Canadian Armed Forces identified four soldiers killed in a fast-moving fire during training at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta: Sgt. Morgan Wong, Pte. Shaun Farrell, Pte. Aidan Goulding and Pte. Hayden Lykkemark. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people were receiving medical care: 19 in critical condition, eight in stable condition and 12 as outpatients [canada.ca#2][globalnews.ca#1][globalnews.ca#2]. Major-General Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division, said a grass fire had been burning nearby but was thought to be contained and far enough away for the exercise to continue. A sudden wind shift drove the flames about a kilometre toward the troops in roughly 30 seconds; officials have not determined what ignited the fire [lethbridgeherald.com#1][theguardian.com#1]. The soldiers belonged to the Edmonton-based 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry, and were training for a rapid-response role and a planned deployment to Latvia next spring. Military and Royal Canadian Mounted Police investigators are examining the cause; Rutland said determining the cause could take weeks. The military said there was no indication of terrorism [globalnews.ca#1][npr.org#1][nagariknetwork.com#1].

items.title: [Dwell] It’s Easy Being Green at This $1.2M Passive House in Minneapolis
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Designed by an architect as his personal residence, the solar-powered building uses 90 percent less energy for heating than typical homes, and it has an envelope that’s about 13 times tighter than code requirements.
